events.continuity_hook: This narrows the Chicago expo plan after the first comparison of airport, hotel area, and possible spouse extension.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the outbound and return flights, decide between the event block and South Loop hotel, drop or keep any extension planning, and list booking steps for seats, room request, transit, and expense notes.
events.scenario_brief: The Chicago expo organizer confirms that Sunday booth setup is now required from mid-afternoon into early evening, and the previously tentative Thursday client breakfast is set for the West Loop before normal checkout time. Erin’s spouse cannot join, so the River North weekend-extension option drops out. The Sunday afternoon arrival she first liked would be too close to setup if O'Hare traffic is heavy, while a late-morning Denver-to-O'Hare nonstop gives better cushion; Midway remains cheaper but less convenient for the convention area and the Thursday return. The event block still has the shortest walk but only higher-rate two-queen rooms with limited amenities, while the South Loop hotel can hold a quiet king room with pool and fitness access but no listed hot tub.

events.continuity_hook: This is the practical logistics pass after Erin settled the Chicago flights and South Loop hotel.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm the Chicago itinerary still works, then organize airport transfer timing, badge pickup, setup-route notes, Thursday breakfast checkout, weather packing, return seat monitoring, and the compact work-bag setup.
events.scenario_brief: Five days before the Chicago departure, Erin has booked the late-morning Sunday nonstop into O'Hare, the Thursday early-afternoon return, and the South Loop hotel through checkout after the client breakfast. No rental car is planned. The expo app now sends badge pickup to a different hall from the setup entrance, a weekend transit notice could slow the train option from O'Hare, and storms may affect the Sunday arrival window. The hotel confirms a room away from elevators plus pool and fitness access, but the hot tub remains unavailable; the outbound window seat is set, while the return seat map has shifted after an aircraft swap.

events.continuity_hook: This starts the next client-training trip after the Chicago conference-style week is off her calendar.
events.interaction_goal: Build a ranked first plan for flight timing, rental car, Portland-only versus split-stay hotels, equipment handling, likely return city, and the clinic confirmations Erin should get before booking.
events.scenario_brief: After the Chicago expo wraps, Erin is assigned a late-August Pacific Northwest clinic rollout with a Monday afternoon handoff near Vancouver, Washington, a Tuesday training on Portland’s east side, a Wednesday session in Salem, and a Thursday hands-on lab in Eugene. A Friday debrief in Portland is still pending. She will be carrying training supplies again, so a rental car with easy parking matters more than staying downtown. A Sunday afternoon nonstop from Denver to Portland gives the calmest start, a Monday morning one-stop is cheaper but fragile for the handoff, and flying into Eugene first would create backtracking. Hotel options include a well-reviewed eastside Portland property with pool and fitness access but no hot tub, a downtown Portland hotel with better dining but expensive parking, and a Eugene final-night property with stronger recovery amenities.

events.continuity_hook: This follows the first Pacific Northwest rollout plan once the clinic times and debrief format become firm.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the return timing, finalize the split-stay hotel plan, set rental-car pickup and drop-off windows, and outline booking steps for seats, parking, room requests, and clinic arrival notes.
events.scenario_brief: The Pacific Northwest clinics confirm the route order: Monday handoff near Vancouver at 3:00 p.m., Tuesday east Portland training at 8:30 a.m., Wednesday Salem session at 10:00 a.m., and Thursday Eugene lab ending around 4:00 p.m.; the Friday debrief will be remote. The Sunday afternoon Denver-to-Portland nonstop now fits best, and the Monday morning one-stop is no longer worth the risk. Lodging has narrowed to the eastside Portland hotel for the first three nights and the Eugene property for the final night, both with parking; the Portland hotel lacks a hot tub, but the Eugene hotel has pool, hot tub, and fitness access. The remaining decision is whether to return late Thursday from Eugene with a connection after the lab or take a calmer Friday morning itinerary with one more hotel night.

events.continuity_hook: This closes the Pacific Northwest planning after Erin chose the calmer Friday return and split-stay hotels.
events.interaction_goal: Run the final logistics pass for road timing, smoke and rain packing, demo-case weight, hotel arrival windows, rental return, airport cushion, seat selection, and the daily clinic folder.
events.scenario_brief: Five days before leaving for the Pacific Northwest rollout, Erin has booked the Sunday afternoon nonstop to Portland, the split hotel plan, a rental car, and a Friday morning return from Eugene with one short connection. Road work on I-5 could affect the Salem-to-Eugene leg, wildfire smoke is possible later in the week, and the Salem clinic asks her to bring an extra box of consumables that may push her checked demo case close to the weight limit. The Portland hotel confirms parking, pool, and fitness access but no hot tub; the Eugene hotel confirms all three amenities. The outbound window seat is selected, but the return connection seat assignment still needs attention.

events.continuity_hook: This shifts from a dense run of work travel into a recovery-focused leisure weekend for two travelers.
events.interaction_goal: Create a ranked shortlist for dates, airport choice, rental car, hotel style, balcony versus wellness amenities, and what to hold while waiting on the spouse’s PTO confirmation.
events.scenario_brief: After the Pacific Northwest rollout, Erin and her spouse start planning a late-September anniversary long weekend in Santa Fe. Their preferred window is Thursday through Sunday if her spouse can take Friday off, with Friday through Monday as the fallback. A Thursday afternoon Denver-to-Santa Fe nonstop is the simplest but priced higher, flying into Albuquerque offers more schedule choices with a rental-car drive, and a Friday evening arrival would cut too much into the weekend. Lodging choices include a downtown boutique inn with balcony rooms and strong reviews but no pool, a resort-style property outside the center with pool, hot tub, fitness access, and easier parking, and a plaza-area hotel with the best walking location but higher valet costs. The PTO answer and how much they want to drive remain unresolved.
